From Puckline Press

Puckline Press article

Frozen Frenzy, explained: the night all 32 NHL teams play

Tuesday's 16-game Frozen Frenzy was the fourth in a row. Here's what the event is, where it came from, how rare it is, and how last night went.

By Puckline Prince · Oct 14, 2026 · Article page

Read the article

Every NHL team played on Tuesday night. That's the Frozen Frenzy: one evening, 16 games, all 32 clubs, and a new puck drop almost every 15 minutes from 6 p.m. Eastern until the last game started at 11. ESPN says this was the fourth year in a row it has put the event on.

The Frozen Frenzy is a scheduling showcase built with ESPN. The league gives the night a full slate, then spreads the start times out so the games overlap as little as possible. ESPN carries a tripleheader on its main channel (6 p.m., 8:30 p.m. and 11 p.m. Eastern), and the other 13 games stream on its services.

The centrepiece is a whip-around studio show that jumps from rink to rink for goals, big hits and late finishes, the hockey version of the NFL's RedZone. In the first edition, John Buccigross and Kevin Weekes hosted it, and the show ran about six and a half hours across ESPN+ and ESPN2.

This year's tripleheader was Devils at Red Wings at 6, Avalanche at Stars at 8:30 and Bruins at Sharks at 11. The other games started every 15 minutes from 6:15 to 9 p.m., then at 9:45 (Flames at Ducks) and 10:30 (Oilers at Kings), so all 16 games had their own start time.

A night with all 32 teams in action is newer than you might think. The first 16-game day in NHL history was Saturday, April 8, 2023, the last Saturday of the 2022-23 regular season. That day started at 12:30 p.m. Eastern and was not branded as anything.

The first Frozen Frenzy came six months later, on Tuesday, Oct. 24, 2023. NHL.com called it the second 16-game day in league history. ESPN's tripleheader that night was Maple Leafs at Capitals, Bruins at Blackhawks (Connor Bedard's rookie season) and Flyers at the Golden Knights, the defending Stanley Cup champions.

Since then it has become a fixture of October:

  • Oct. 24, 2023: the first Frozen Frenzy
  • Oct. 22, 2024: opened with Capitals at Flyers, closed with Kings at Golden Knights
  • Oct. 28, 2025: opened with Penguins at Flyers, closed with Kings at Sharks
  • Oct. 13, 2026: opened with Devils at Red Wings, closed with Bruins at Sharks

All four have been on a Tuesday.

Nights like this are rare. Before the 2024 edition, NHL.com counted only three earlier days with all 32 teams playing: April 8, 2023, the first Frozen Frenzy, and Jan. 13, 2024. It also said the 2024 Frenzy would be the only day that season with every team in action.

So the Frenzy is the one guaranteed 16-game night on the calendar, and in some seasons it has been the only one.

The 2026 edition delivered 112 goals in 16 games, an average of seven a game. Road teams won nine of the 16. Three games went past regulation: the Devils won in overtime in Detroit, 5-4, and the Canadiens (over Buffalo, 4-3) and Kraken (in Philadelphia, 3-2) both won in shootouts.

All the final scores:

  • Devils 5, Red Wings 4 (OT)
  • Panthers 7, Blue Jackets 3
  • Canadiens 4, Sabres 3 (SO)
  • Hurricanes 4, Capitals 2
  • Kraken 3, Flyers 2 (SO)
  • Rangers 4, Lightning 1
  • Blues 7, Senators 2
  • Islanders 3, Canucks 2
  • Blackhawks 5, Penguins 3
  • Jets 5, Wild 2
  • Avalanche 3, Stars 2
  • Golden Knights 5, Predators 2
  • Mammoth 5, Maple Leafs 4
  • Flames 4, Ducks 2
  • Oilers 4, Kings 1
  • Bruins 6, Sharks 3

The most lopsided results were Florida's 7-3 win in Columbus and St. Louis's 7-2 win in Ottawa. In the 8:30 headliner, Colorado beat Dallas 3-2 in regulation, and Boston closed the night with six goals in San Jose.

Full recaps of every game are on the Last night page.

Tuesday, November 3

Game recap

VGK2BOS3SOFinal: VGK 2, BOS 3 SO

Vegas spent two periods digging a hole at TD Garden, climbed all the way out, then forgot how to shoot a puck one-on-one. Rookie James Hagens opened the scoring in the first, his sixth of the year, and Morgan Geekie made it 2-0 on the power play early in the second. Braeden Bowman was ejected early in the second for elbowing Matthew Poitras, who didn't return. Mark Stone answered on a Vegas power play and Trevor Connelly tied it 7:23 into the third, with Mitch Marner setting up both for two assists. Overtime settled nothing, so it went to a shootout, where Connelly, Jack Eichel and Marner all came up empty against Jeremy Swayman (21 saves on 23 in regulation and OT) and David Pastrnak, after seven shots and no goal all night, finally found the net with Boston's last shooter. Carter Hart stopped 25 of 27 and got a loser's point for it. Boston moves to 11-4-1. Vegas goes to Pittsburgh tonight with three of the league's best hands, and not one of them could beat a goalie from 30 feet.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET5FLA3Final: DET 5, FLA 3

Detroit flew south and gave the two-time champs a lesson in finishing. Carter Mazur, playing all of 7:26, scored his first NHL goal in the first, and Sam Reinhart answered for Florida. Alex DeBrincat put the Wings back in front early in the second, then Aaron Ekblad tied it shorthanded, a goal so rare for him it was his first of the season. The third took 45 seconds to decide: Justin Faulk scored on the power play at 2:08 and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård followed at 2:53, adding seven hits for a two-point night. Sam Bennett made it 4-3 with Jacob Markstrom pulled, and Emmitt Finnie sealed it with an empty-netter three seconds from the end. Daniil Tarasov, starting against his old team, made 23 saves on 26 and Markstrom 24 on 28. Detroit goes to 7-5-3 and on to Tampa tonight. Florida dressed both Tkachuk brothers and still lost to a guy whose NHL goal total went from zero to one.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL5CHI2Final: COL 5, CHI 2

For about 15 minutes the United Center got to feel like it was 2013 again. Wyatt Kaiser scored 57 seconds in and Roman Kantserov made it 2-0 at 7:05 off a Connor Bedard feed. Then Colorado remembered it was Colorado. Nazem Kadri and Jaden Schwartz scored 26 seconds apart late in the first to tie it, Kadri added a power-play goal in the second off Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon, and Schwartz scored again with 11 seconds left in the period for two goals each. Devon Toews finished it into an empty net. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 21 of 23 after the early hiccup, while Spencer Knight made 24 saves on 28. The Avalanche move to 9-5-1 and play in Columbus tonight. Chicago falls to 4-10-1: two goals up in seven minutes, five unanswered against, and the rebuild keeps finding new ways to lose.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY2SJS1Final: CGY 2, SJS 1

Calgary won a game in San Jose with its depth forwards doing the scoring and Dustin Wolf doing everything else. Adam Klapka scored in the first off Jonathan Castagna, then set up William Stromgren's first of the season midway through the third, with Castagna on that one too. Neither of them played 12 minutes, and they still outscored the Sharks' whole top six. Sam Dickinson got San Jose on the board less than three minutes later, but Wolf, who made 26 saves on 27, shut the door from there. Yaroslav Askarov was solid at the other end with 20 saves on 22. The Flames improve to 7-8-0. The Sharks drop to 7-8-1 with a fourth loss in five games, and Dickinson admitted there's frustration in the room. When your best chance is a defenseman's first goal of the year and the other team's grinders are running the show, the frustration makes sense.

Monday, November 2

Game recap

WPG0CAR7Final: WPG 0, CAR 7

Carolina hosted Winnipeg on Sunday and ran it like a practice with fans. Sean Walker opened the scoring shorthanded at 5:16 of the first, and then the Hurricanes put up four goals in 7:14 of the second: Juuso Välimäki, Sebastian Aho on the power play, Walker again, and Logan Stankoven for his 10th. Stuart Skinner was pulled after 12 saves on 17 shots, and Clay Stevenson gave up two more in the third to Mark Jankowski (power play) and Jesperi Kotkaniemi. At the other end, Pyotr Kochetkov had a quiet night: 26 saves and a shutout. Carolina is 12-2-2 with 26 points, the most in the league. Winnipeg is 0-7-2 in its last nine, and the hot seat in that building is starting to need its own Zamboni.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN5WSH1Final: MIN 5, WSH 1

Minnesota came into Washington without Brock Faber or Jared Spurgeon and still treated the Capitals like the undercard. Quinn Hughes scored 3:42 in, Michael McCarron added another 1:45 later, and the Wild sat on 2-0 until Justin Sourdif got one back with six seconds left in the second. That was all Washington got off Jesper Wallstedt, who stopped 26 of 27. Then the third turned into a fire sale: Maxim Shabanov scored on the power play, Kirill Kaprizov hit the empty net for his 15th of the season, and Danila Yurov added another power-play goal with 25 seconds left. Logan Thompson made 24 saves on 28 shots. The Wild are 10-3-3 and first in the Central. Washington's offense showed up for six seconds, so maybe that Larkin phone call to Detroit should go out sooner rather than later.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA3PHI6Final: UTA 3, PHI 6

Travis Konecny came back from 10 games on IR and the league's lowest-scoring team suddenly found six. Matvei Michkov opened it with his 10th, Dmitri Simashev answered for Utah, and Konecny scored his first of the season 1:06 into the second. Noah Cates, Christian Dvorak and Oliver Bonk made it 5-1 by 5:35 of the third. Utah's power play woke up late, with Mikhail Sergachev scoring and then Logan Cooley with the goalie pulled, before Cole Knuble iced it into the empty net. Lawson Crouse and Simon Benoit fought in the third. Dan Vladar made 19 saves, and Karel Vejmelka stopped 15 of 20. Utah gave up five goals on 20 shots to the team that scores the fewest in the league, which is a bit like losing a footrace to a guy carrying a couch.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM4NYR1Final: EDM 4, NYR 1

Connor McDavid scored 50 seconds in, and the Rangers spent the rest of the night chasing the bus. Evan Bouchard set up McDavid and Colton Dach in the opening 6:19, then scored on the power play in the second. His goal and two assists make him the fourth defenseman with 25 or more points through a season's first 15 games, alongside Bobby Orr, Al MacInnis and Denis Potvin. Pavel Dorofeyev scored for New York, and Dach hit the empty net for his first multigoal NHL game. Matt Tomkins won his Oilers debut with 27 saves on 28 shots; Dylan Garand made 21. Edmonton is 11-2-2 and 7-0-0 on the road, and McDavid has 39 points. The Rangers have lost four straight, and the Garden crowd is now paying Broadway prices for a show that closes in the first act.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT3ANA6Final: OTT 3, ANA 6

Ottawa led 3-0 after one period in Anaheim and then forgot there were two more. Philip Tomasino, Claude Giroux and Michael Amadio scored in the first, but Cutter Gauthier and Judd Caulfield cut it to 3-2 early in the second, and Caulfield tied it on the power play with 42 seconds left in the period. The third was a power-play clinic: Gauthier scored twice in 36 seconds to finish a hat trick, and Roger McQueen added a fourth power-play goal for the night. Leo Carlsson had three assists. Dylan Cozens was ejected after a long video review for a blindside hit on A.J. Greer. Laurent Brossoit made 19 saves on 22 shots, and Jonas Johansson stopped 27 of 33. Blowing a three-goal lead on the road isn't a collapse in Ottawa, it's a franchise tradition with a logo.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

nhl.com ↗
SJS
Lineup

Update: Toffoli moves up with Celebrini and Smith against Calgary, Stenberg to the third line; Askarov starts

At Monday's morning skate the Sharks went Toffoli-Celebrini-Smith and Stenberg-Bystedt-Graf, and Ryan Warsofsky said Toffoli has earned the spot. Will Smith plays the point on a five-forward top power play, and Yaroslav Askarov is expected in goal rather than Nedeljkovic.

Confirmed · Nov 2: Yaroslav Askarov started in goal for San Jose against Calgary. espn.com ↗

Lineup

With Malkin out, Kuzmenko moves onto Kindel's line; Brazeau skates with Koivunen and Lapierre

At Monday's practice the Penguins skated Kuzmenko-Kindel-Chinakhov, with Chinakhov on the right side, and Koivunen-Lapierre-Brazeau. Rakell-Crosby-Rust stayed together.

Lineup

Devils change their power play: Connor Brown moves up to PP1 and Evangelista drops to PP2

At Monday's practice the top unit was Luke Hughes, Jack Hughes, Hischier, Bratt and Brown, and the second Hamilton, Meier, Gritsyuk, Evangelista and Mantha. The power play ranks 24th at 16.7 percent.

Lineup

Update: Shane Wright centers Forsberg and Hoglander at practice ahead of his Predators debut Tuesday against Carolina

Wright skated as the second-line center between Filip Forsberg and Nils Hoglander on Monday. Brunette wants him at center and hopes he becomes a top-six forward who brings pace through the middle.

si.com ↗
TOR
Lineup

Cowan back on the top line with Matthews and Roslovic; Joshua moves up and McKenna drops to the third line

At Monday's practice Easton Cowan rejoined Auston Matthews and Jack Roslovic, Dakota Joshua moved up with Nick Paul and William Nylander, and Gavin McKenna went to the third line with Colton Sissons and Vinni Lettieri. Jim Hiller said the team wanted that line back together.

sports.yahoo.com ↗
SEA
Lineup

Botterill says new Kraken forward Matthew Wood will start at right wing

GM Jason Botterill said Wood, acquired from Nashville for Shane Wright, will start on the wing and could move around, praising his reach, shot and hockey sense. Wood is a restricted free agent after the season.

nhl.com ↗
NYR
Lineup

Rangers reshuffle again after four straight losses: Will Cuylle tries centre, Perreault moves up with J.T. Miller

At Monday's practice Mike Sullivan kept only the Dorofeyev-Zibanejad-Lafreniere line together. Cuylle, who has never played centre, led a new third line with Eeli Tolvanen, Gabe Perreault moved up with Miller and Noah Laba dropped to the fourth line ahead of Tuesday's game with St. Louis.

Monday's practice lines for Tuesday in Anaheim: DeBrusk-Pettersson-Boeser, Ohgren-Rossi-Lekkerimaki, O'Connor-Quillan-Karlsson and Cotter-Sasson-Gallagher, with Bains extra. Practice lines, not a confirmed lineup.

Maple Leafs put Bo Groulx on waivers after he dressed for one of their last seven games

Toronto placed centre Bo Groulx on waivers Monday. He has no points in seven games this season and missed Monday's practice. He is a pending UFA with an $812,500 cap hit.

Dylan McIlrath clears waivers and heads to AHL Hershey

The Capitals defenseman went unclaimed Monday after Washington waived him to make room for goalie Rémi Poirier. He will join the Hershey Bears.

VGK 2–3 BOS SO

Vegas Golden KnightsVGK9-5-2 · 20 pts23 shots
2
Final/SOTD Garden
3
Boston BruinsBOS11-4-1 · 23 pts27 shots
1st2nd3rdOTSOTVGK011002BOS110013

Puckline's Report

Vegas spent two periods digging a hole at TD Garden, climbed all the way out, then forgot how to shoot a puck one-on-one. Rookie James Hagens opened the scoring in the first, his sixth of the year, and Morgan Geekie made it 2-0 on the power play early in the second. Braeden Bowman was ejected early in the second for elbowing Matthew Poitras, who didn't return. Mark Stone answered on a Vegas power play and Trevor Connelly tied it 7:23 into the third, with Mitch Marner setting up both for two assists. Overtime settled nothing, so it went to a shootout, where Connelly, Jack Eichel and Marner all came up empty against Jeremy Swayman (21 saves on 23 in regulation and OT) and David Pastrnak, after seven shots and no goal all night, finally found the net with Boston's last shooter. Carter Hart stopped 25 of 27 and got a loser's point for it. Boston moves to 11-4-1. Vegas goes to Pittsburgh tonight with three of the league's best hands, and not one of them could beat a goalie from 30 feet.

DET 5–3 FLA

Detroit Red WingsDET7-5-3 · 17 pts29 shots
5
FinalAmerant Bank Arena
3
Florida PanthersFLA8-5-2 · 18 pts26 shots
1st2nd3rdTDET1135FLA1113

Puckline's Report

Detroit flew south and gave the two-time champs a lesson in finishing. Carter Mazur, playing all of 7:26, scored his first NHL goal in the first, and Sam Reinhart answered for Florida. Alex DeBrincat put the Wings back in front early in the second, then Aaron Ekblad tied it shorthanded, a goal so rare for him it was his first of the season. The third took 45 seconds to decide: Justin Faulk scored on the power play at 2:08 and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård followed at 2:53, adding seven hits for a two-point night. Sam Bennett made it 4-3 with Jacob Markstrom pulled, and Emmitt Finnie sealed it with an empty-netter three seconds from the end. Daniil Tarasov, starting against his old team, made 23 saves on 26 and Markstrom 24 on 28. Detroit goes to 7-5-3 and on to Tampa tonight. Florida dressed both Tkachuk brothers and still lost to a guy whose NHL goal total went from zero to one.

Puckline's Report

For about 15 minutes the United Center got to feel like it was 2013 again. Wyatt Kaiser scored 57 seconds in and Roman Kantserov made it 2-0 at 7:05 off a Connor Bedard feed. Then Colorado remembered it was Colorado. Nazem Kadri and Jaden Schwartz scored 26 seconds apart late in the first to tie it, Kadri added a power-play goal in the second off Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon, and Schwartz scored again with 11 seconds left in the period for two goals each. Devon Toews finished it into an empty net. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 21 of 23 after the early hiccup, while Spencer Knight made 24 saves on 28. The Avalanche move to 9-5-1 and play in Columbus tonight. Chicago falls to 4-10-1: two goals up in seven minutes, five unanswered against, and the rebuild keeps finding new ways to lose.

By Puckline Prince

Puckline's Report

Calgary won a game in San Jose with its depth forwards doing the scoring and Dustin Wolf doing everything else. Adam Klapka scored in the first off Jonathan Castagna, then set up William Stromgren's first of the season midway through the third, with Castagna on that one too. Neither of them played 12 minutes, and they still outscored the Sharks' whole top six. Sam Dickinson got San Jose on the board less than three minutes later, but Wolf, who made 26 saves on 27, shut the door from there. Yaroslav Askarov was solid at the other end with 20 saves on 22. The Flames improve to 7-8-0. The Sharks drop to 7-8-1 with a fourth loss in five games, and Dickinson admitted there's frustration in the room. When your best chance is a defenseman's first goal of the year and the other team's grinders are running the show, the frustration makes sense.

By Puckline Prince

UTA @ TOR · 7:00 PM ET

Utah MammothUTA9-6-0 · 18 PTSML -134
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 3 · Scotiabank Arena
UTA -134MLTOR +112
Toronto Maple LeafsTOR8-6-2 · 18 PTSML +112

Puckline Preview

The last time Utah came to Scotiabank Arena, on Oct. 13, the Mammoth left with a 5-4 win and handed Anthony Stolarz his only loss of the season. So naturally Stolarz sits tonight. Jim Hiller confirmed Sergei Bobrovsky starts, sticking to a goalie plan he says was set in the summer, which means a .885 save percentage gets the net over a guy who has won three straight. Plans are plans. Toronto opens a six-game homestand with Easton Cowan back alongside Auston Matthews and Jack Roslovic, who has points in six straight games. Matthews has 11 goals and a point in all eight road games, so the Leafs would love that to follow him home. Rookie Gavin McKenna drops to the third line, and John Tavares has been upgraded to day to day after skating with the team in a non-contact jersey, but he isn't in tonight's lineup.

Utah brings the league's most dangerous power play (18 goals, 34.6%) and Logan Cooley, who has scored in three straight games. It also brings Sunday's 6-3 loss in Philadelphia, after which Mikhail Sergachev said the team cheated out of its own zone. TSN reports Sebastian Cossa is in line to start over Karel Vejmelka (.871), so both nets carry some suspense.

By Puckline Prince

WPG @ MTL · 7:00 PM ET

Winnipeg JetsWPG4-8-3 · 11 PTSML +160
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 3 · Centre Bell
WPG +160MLMTL -194
Montreal CanadiensMTL9-3-2 · 20 PTSML -194

Puckline Preview

Nine days ago these two played the Heritage Classic outdoors in Winnipeg, and Montreal won 2-1 behind 33 saves from Jacob Fowler. The Jets haven't won since. Make that nine straight without a win (0-7-2), five of them by one goal, with the other team scoring first in six straight. Sunday's 7-0 loss in Carolina, where Stuart Skinner was pulled after five goals on 17 shots, was the low point; Scott Arniel called it pretty embarrassing for the organization. Captain Adam Lowry says changes are coming if this keeps up, and Arniel says his job security isn't on his mind. Arniel still hasn't said who starts in goal for Winnipeg tonight, only that it won't be Nico Daws, which tells you something too. Josh Morrissey is aiming for Sunday, not tonight.

Montreal, meanwhile, is having a very different autumn: five straight wins, new Hometown Remix jerseys, and Fowler, the NHL's rookie of the month for October (7-1-0, .932, two shutouts), with seven straight wins of his own. Nick Suzuki skated back on the top line with Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovsky Monday, but he won't play tonight, his sixth straight game out, and Kirby Dach is still sick and out too. The Bell Centre gets a slumping team from the Prairies. It knows what to do with one.

By Puckline Prince

DET @ TBL · 7:00 PM ET

Detroit Red WingsDET7-5-3 · 17 PTSML +210
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 3 · Benchmark International Arena
DET +210MLTBL -260
Tampa Bay LightningTBL8-3-2 · 18 PTSML -260

Puckline Preview

Welcome to the Unhappy Stars Bowl. Detroit suspended Dylan Larkin without pay after he told the team he won't play for the Red Wings again, and Nikita Kucherov has asked Tampa Bay for a trade, saying it was never about money but about communication and respect. (Friedman reports he wanted something in the range of Kirill Kaprizov's $17 million a year, so the money may have come up once or twice.) GM Julien BriseBois says he has no intention of trading him. Friedman also says someone floated a one-for-one Larkin-for-Kucherov swap to him, while stressing nothing suggests the teams have talked. Imagine the handshake line.

On the ice, Kucherov had three assists in his first game after the request and has 58 career points in 43 games against Detroit, a franchise record. Andrei Vasilevskiy is 19-5-2 with a .929 against the Wings, though he's at .876 this season. Detroit plays the second night of a back-to-back after a 5-3 win in Florida that featured Carter Mazur's first NHL goal. John Gibson (.860) is the likely starter after allowing five goals on 15 shots in a blown 4-2 third-period lead against St. Louis. Todd McLellan says don't pin that one on him, which is a nice thing to say about a .860.

By Puckline Prince

STL @ NYR · 7:00 PM ET

St Louis BluesSTL7-6-1 · 15 PTSML +100
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 3 · Madison Square Garden
STL +100MLNYR -120
New York RangersNYR7-7-1 · 15 PTSML -120

Puckline Preview

The Rangers have lost four straight, the latest a 4-1 loss to Edmonton on Sunday, and Mike Sullivan has done what coaches do when they've run out of answers: he put the lines in a blender. Only Dorofeyev-Zibanejad-Lafreniere survived Monday's practice. Gabe Perreault moved up with J.T. Miller, Noah Laba dropped to the fourth line, and Will Cuylle is playing centre for the first time in his life. Nothing says "we've got this figured out" like teaching a winger to take faceoffs in November. With Igor Shesterkin out for the season, rookie Dylan Garand (.897) carries the crease; Adam Fox leads the team with 17 points and Alexis Lafreniere has nine goals.

St. Louis arrives on a two-game win streak after coming back from 4-2 down in the third in Detroit, with Aleksanteri Kaskimaki's first NHL goal as the winner. Jimmy Snuggerud leads the Blues with eight goals, and ex-Ranger Pavel Buchnevich has seven points in nine games against his old team. Joel Hofer (.916, 2.42) is the projected starter, and Colton Parayko is questionable. New York swept last season's series, but the Blues are 4-2-1 in their last seven against them, and right now the Rangers would take a draw.

By Puckline Prince

MIN @ PHI · 7:00 PM ET

Minnesota WildMIN10-3-3 · 23 PTSML -176
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 3 · Xfinity Mobile Arena
MIN -176MLPHI +146
Philadelphia FlyersPHI4-8-4 · 12 PTSML +146

Puckline Preview

Kirill Kaprizov had the kind of October that gets a man an eight-figure raise. Oh wait, he already got one. He scored 14 goals and 24 points in 15 games, tying the Wild's record for goals in a month and becoming the first player with 14 October goals since Alex Ovechkin in 2009, then reached 500 career points with an empty-netter Sunday in Washington. Minnesota is first in the Central at 10-3-3 on a five-game point streak, and it's doing it without Brock Faber, Jared Spurgeon, Filip Gustavsson and both Folignos. Jesper Wallstedt (9-2-3, .919) is the likely starter, which is bad news for a Flyers team scoring 2.19 goals a game, the fewest in the league.

Philadelphia did just put six on Utah, with Travis Konecny scoring in his return from IR, and Matvei Michkov has 10 goals. Last week Sean Couturier said the Flyers are soft at times; Rick Tocchet says they're not soft, just hesitant, which is the kind of distinction only a coach could love. One thing in Philly's favour: it won the last two meetings, both past regulation, including a 3-2 shootout win in March where Konecny scored the only shootout goal on Wallstedt. In goal, Tocchet hasn't said whether it's Dan Vladar again or Joseph Woll, and he's thinking about ending the rotation altogether.

By Puckline Prince

VGK @ PIT · 7:00 PM ET

Vegas Golden KnightsVGK9-5-2 · 20 PTSML -110
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 3 · PPG Paints Arena
VGK -110MLPIT -110
Pittsburgh PenguinsPIT5-7-2 · 12 PTSML -110

Puckline Preview

Vegas arrives in Pittsburgh on the second night of a back-to-back, still sore from a shootout in Boston where Jack Eichel, Mitch Marner and Trevor Connelly all missed and David Pastrnak didn't. Marner's point streak is up to 10 games, Braeden Bowman was tossed for elbowing Matthew Poitras, and Carter Hart played all 65 minutes, so Adin Hill (5-2-0) is the likely starter. Hill was also in net on Oct. 17, when Vegas beat the Penguins 6-2 and scored twice in the first four minutes.

Pittsburgh's season is a museum with a hospital wing. Sidney Crosby just passed Ray Bourque for the most assists with one franchise and is tied with Marcel Dionne for sixth all-time with 1,771 points, and Erik Karlsson passed Brent Burns for 10th in career points by a defenseman. But Evgeni Malkin and Kaedan Korczak are day to day, Bryan Rust and Elmer Soderblom are on IR, and Justin Brazeau makes his season debut with Andrei Kuzmenko moving into the top six. Arturs Silovs is the projected starter. The Penguins are 5-7-2 and 3-5-2 in their last 10, so the history is great; the present is a work in progress.

By Puckline Prince

DAL @ WSH · 7:00 PM ET

Dallas StarsDAL8-5-1 · 17 PTSML -110
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 3 · Capital One Arena
DAL -110MLWSH -110
Washington CapitalsWSH8-5-0 · 16 PTSML -110

Puckline Preview

Washington has three goalies on the roster and a coach who can't say for how long. After trading a seventh-round pick for Remi Poirier, Spencer Carbery said the setup could last 48 hours or three months, which is the hockey version of "we'll see." Logan Thompson (.898) is expected to start, with Charlie Lindgren backing up and Poirier watching. The Caps are also coming off a 5-1 loss to Minnesota in which Tom Wilson took 14 penalty minutes and Carbery accused Zach Bogosian of selling a high stick, and LeBrun reports they've talked to Detroit about Dylan Larkin. Alex Tuch leads them with 10 goals, five of them game-winners.

Dallas owns this matchup lately: 8-1-0 in the last nine against Washington, with Roope Hintz on an eight-game point streak against the Caps and Tyler Seguin at 23 points in 32 career games against them. The Stars allow a league-low 22.3 shots a game, their penalty kill runs at 93.6%, and Jake Oettinger (1.63 GAA, .921) is the likely starter. Radek Faksa should be back. Glen Gulutzan says the six-game homestand ran too long and the team got mentally tired, so a road trip is apparently the cure. Washington's 17.6% power play hopes he's wrong.

COL @ CBJ · 7:00 PM ET

Colorado AvalancheCOL9-5-1 · 19 PTSML -132
@7:00 PM ETTue Nov 3 · Nationwide Arena
COL -132MLCBJ +110
Columbus Blue JacketsCBJ5-7-0 · 10 PTSML +110

Puckline Preview

Colorado plays the second night of a back-to-back after spotting Chicago a 2-0 lead and then scoring the last five goals, with Nazem Kadri and Jaden Schwartz scoring twice each and Kadri reaching 100 career power-play goals. Cale Makar took a high elbow from Artyom Levshunov and stayed in the game, and Jared Bednar's 453rd win with the Avalanche moved him past Joel Quenneville for ninth in wins with one franchise. With Mackenzie Blackwood playing all 60 minutes Monday, Scott Wedgewood (1-2-1, .889) is the likely starter. Colorado scores 4.27 goals a game, tied with Edmonton for the league lead, even with Josh Manson out about eight weeks.

Columbus is last in the Metropolitan at 5-7-0 with one regulation win all season, tied with Vancouver for the fewest in the league. It managed 15 shots in a 3-1 loss in Dallas on Saturday, and Rick Bowness insists the team will go on a run if the effort holds. Chris Johnston ranks Dmitri Voronkov third on his trade board (reported). Jet Greaves (2-5-0) is the projected starter. Colorado won both meetings last season by a combined 8-1, including a 4-0 shutout in January with Brent Burns scoring twice, so the run Bowness wants might start against somebody else.

By Puckline Prince

EDM @ NJD · 7:30 PM ET

Edmonton OilersEDM11-2-2 · 24 PTSML +128
@7:30 PM ETTue Nov 3 · Prudential Center
EDM +128MLNJD -154
New Jersey DevilsNJD9-5-0 · 18 PTSML -154

Puckline Preview

Edmonton is 7-0-0 on the road and goes for an eighth straight road win to start the season, having allowed one goal across its last three games: two Tristan Jarry shutouts and a 4-1 win at Madison Square Garden with Matt Tomkins in net. Connor McDavid has a point in all 15 games (9 goals, 30 assists) and an assist in every one of them, an NHL record to open a season. He, Leon Draisaitl (28) and Evan Bouchard (26) have the most points by three teammates through 15 games since 1996-97. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins plays his 1,038th game as an Oiler tonight, passing Kevin Lowe for the franchise record. Zach Hyman and Devon Levi are questionable.

New Jersey has won the last four meetings, five of its last six games, and hasn't lost at home since Oct. 12. The Devils also have Connor Hellebuyck now, 2-0 since the Oct. 23 trade from Winnipeg. Their power play is 24th (16.7%), so Sheldon Keefe moved former Oiler Connor Brown to the first unit. Bratt pointed to Brown's experience playing with McDavid and Draisaitl, which is a polite way of saying "he's seen how it's done." The penalty kill is 25th at 70%, and that's the scary part against this power play.

By Puckline Prince

CAR @ NSH · 8:00 PM ET

Carolina HurricanesCAR12-2-2 · 26 PTSML -192
@8:00 PM ETTue Nov 3 · Bridgestone Arena
CAR -192MLNSH +158
Nashville PredatorsNSH5-4-5 · 15 PTSML +158

Puckline Preview

Pyotr Kochetkov has won all 10 of his starts, joining Carey Price and Jack Campbell as the only goalies to win a season's first 10, and his 7-0 shutout of Winnipeg on Sunday was the 13th of his career. Carolina is 12-2-2 with the league's best record and goal difference, on a four-game win streak, and 30 of its 63 goals have come in second periods, the most by any team in any period. The Hurricanes are still without Jordan Staal and Taylor Hall, and they don't seem to have noticed.

Nashville gets a new face: Shane Wright makes his Predators debut two days after the trade that sent Matthew Wood to Seattle, centring Filip Forsberg (team-high 17 points) and Nils Hoglander. The Preds are 5-4-5, which means five losses past regulation already, so they're very good at getting to overtime and less good at what happens after. Their special teams are strong (power play fifth at 31.9%, penalty kill fourth at 88.9%), and Steven Stamkos just tied Phil Esposito for sixth in career power-play goals with 246. Friedman expects Ryan O'Reilly to be a trade target as Nashville retools. Carolina swept last season's series, and Juuse Saros (3-3-4) is the likely starter for a team that needs a regulation win more than a tiebreaker.

By Puckline Prince

ANA @ VAN · 9:00 PM ET

Anaheim DucksANA6-7-1 · 13 PTSML -150
@9:00 PM ETTue Nov 3 · Rogers Arena
ANA -150MLVAN +125
Vancouver CanucksVAN3-12-1 · 7 PTSML +125

Puckline Preview

These two met a week ago in Anaheim and produced the wildest game of Vancouver's season. Down 5-2 in the third, the Canucks got two goals in 49 seconds from Jonathan Lekkerimaki, the tying one with 1:57 left and the goalie pulled, and Filip Hronek won it 6-5 on a 5-on-3 with 11 seconds left in overtime, ending a 10-game losing streak. That's still one of only three Vancouver wins all season. The Canucks are 3-12-1, last in the league, have lost five straight at home and allow a league-worst 4.50 goals a game. Their best news: they're 8-2-0 in the last 10 against Anaheim, and Brock Boeser has a nine-game point streak against the Ducks.

Anaheim allows 3.79 a game, 30th, so there may not be a lot of defense in the building on Diwali Night at Rogers Arena. The Ducks do have the second-best power play (34.0%), Leo Carlsson with a team-high 21 points after a seven-assist week, and Cutter Gauthier, whose hat trick led six straight goals from 3-0 down against Ottawa on Sunday. Laurent Brossoit won that one and may start again, but Anaheim hasn't said. Friedman reports Jake DeBrusk would welcome a move out of Vancouver; for now he's on the top line with Elias Pettersson and Boeser.

By Puckline Prince
